ingredientSections.heading: Corned Beef
items: 2 Tbsp Yellow or Brown Mustard Seeds
1 Leek, roughly chopped, save the green tops

methodSections.heading: Corned Beef
steps: In a fry pan over a medium heat toast the whole spices for 3 to 4 minutes and then, in a bowl, mix them with the other dry spices.

In a medium sized saucepan combine two tablespoons of the spice mix with the one litre of water, the beer, garlic, salt, sugar and bay leaves, bring this spiced brine to a boil, and then cool and set aside.

Place the brisket in large lidded container, add the cold brine and enough water to cover the meat. Ensure the meat is fully submerged by using a plate or similar to weigh it down. Store in the fridge for a minimum of 3 days and up to 10 days.

Remove the brisket from brine, give it a rinse under cold water and place in a Dutch oven or large pot. Cover it with water and add the remaining spice blend, carrot, onion, leek, and celery. Place pot on the stove, bring up to a boil, then turn down to a low simmer and cook for 2½-3 hours or until tender.

methodSections.heading: Beer Braised Endive
steps: Place the endives cut side down in a hot fry pan with a splash of olive oil. When caramelized, add the sugar, thyme, and some good pinches of salt.
When the sugar starts to brown deglaze with the beer. Once reduced to a liquor remove endives from pan. Turn face up and crust with the toasted breadcrumbs, chives and lemon zest.

methodSections.heading: Beer Mustard
steps: Mix both types of mustard seeds in a small bowl. Stir in the vinegar and beer until just combined. Cover the mixture with plastic wrap and set in a cool, dry place for 12 hours or until all the liquid has been absorbed.
Stir the remaining ingredients into the mustard seed mixture and then pulse in a food processor 5 to 6 times before blending for a minute.
Pour the mixture into a sterilized glass jar and refrigerate. For a spicier result, leave the jar of mustard at room temperature for 1 to 2 days before refrigerating.

methodSections.heading: Garnishes
steps: Bake the green parts of the leek in the oven at 200°C (400°F) until black and dry. Pulse in a blender until it is a fine powder.
Sous-vide an egg, at 63°C for an hour in its shell, remove the egg white and serve the yolk. You could also use a poached egg.
Other garnishes: Nasturtium Leaves, Purslane Leaves, Heirloom Cherry Tomatoes, Cilantro Flowers, Bronze Fennel and Veal Demi Glacé for sauce (buy from your butcher).
